title: Advanced Statistics, Epidemiology and Clinical Research Analytics
description: Twelve practical challenges for reproducible clinical data analysis in Python and R.

challenges.title: Descriptive statistics and data distributions
challenges.scenario: Summarise continuous and categorical clinical variables, inspect skewness and outliers, and distinguish mean/SD from median/IQR.
challenges.tasks: Create a cohort profile by treatment group. Report n, missingness, mean and SD for approximately symmetric variables, median and IQR for skewed variables, and counts/percentages for categorical variables.
challenges.method: Use pandas describe, groupby, value_counts and matplotlib histograms/boxplots. Confirm units and plausible ranges before interpreting.
challenges.acceptance: A table includes denominators and missingness; each summary statistic matches the distribution and measurement scale.
challenges.safety: Outliers must be investigated, not automatically deleted. A boxplot flag is not proof of an error.

challenges.title: Probability, sampling and confidence intervals
challenges.scenario: Explain sampling variability, standard error, confidence intervals and the difference between a confidence interval and a prediction interval.
challenges.tasks: Estimate a mean difference in follow-up SBP between groups with a 95% confidence interval. Interpret the interval in clinical units and explain repeated-sampling meaning.
challenges.method: Implement an independent-group mean difference and bootstrap percentile interval. Compare with a parametric interval and state assumptions.
challenges.acceptance: The point estimate, interval, group sizes and units are reproducible; interpretation avoids saying there is a 95% probability that this fixed parameter lies in the observed interval.
challenges.safety: A narrow interval can still describe biased or non-representative data.

challenges.title: Hypothesis testing and effect sizes
challenges.scenario: Choose tests based on design, variable type, independence, distribution and expected counts; report effect sizes and uncertainty.
challenges.tasks: Compare follow-up SBP between two independent groups. Report the mean difference, 95% CI, p-value and standardised effect size. Explain multiplicity and why p<0.05 is not a clinical decision rule.
challenges.method: Use Welch's t-test, Mann–Whitney U as a sensitivity analysis, and Cohen's d/Hedges' g. State assumptions and the prespecified primary comparison.
challenges.acceptance: The analysis identifies the test, assumptions, effect estimate, CI and p-value; interpretation does not equate statistical significance with clinical importance.
challenges.safety: Do not select a test solely from a normality-test p-value. Inspect design and distributions.

challenges.title: Categorical data and association
challenges.scenario: Use contingency tables, chi-square and Fisher's exact test; quantify association with risk difference, risk ratio and odds ratio.
challenges.tasks: Compare the synthetic event flag across treatment groups. Construct a 2×2 table and report denominators, proportions and an appropriate association measure.
challenges.method: Use scipy.stats chi2_contingency or fisher_exact; compute risk difference and risk ratio with confidence intervals where supported.
challenges.acceptance: Counts reconcile to the source cohort; sparse cells trigger an exact method or justified alternative; reference category is explicit.
challenges.safety: This simulated binary event is not a validated clinical endpoint.

challenges.title: Correlation and linear regression
challenges.scenario: Distinguish correlation from causation; fit and diagnose linear regression; interpret coefficients, residuals, confounding and interactions.
challenges.tasks: Model follow-up SBP using treatment group, baseline SBP, age and diabetes. Interpret adjusted coefficients with units and confidence intervals.
challenges.method: Fit OLS using statsmodels; inspect residual-versus-fitted and Q-Q plots, multicollinearity indicators and influential observations.
challenges.acceptance: Model formula, reference levels, N, coefficients, CIs and diagnostics are recorded; limitations and residual assumptions are stated.
challenges.safety: Adjustment does not remove unmeasured confounding or convert observational associations into causal effects.

challenges.title: Logistic regression and clinical risk modelling
challenges.scenario: Fit logistic regression, interpret odds ratios, assess calibration and discrimination, and avoid leakage/overfitting.
challenges.tasks: Model the synthetic event indicator using age, diabetes, CKD and treatment group. Report odds ratios, calibration plot, ROC-AUC and confusion matrix at a prespecified threshold.
challenges.method: Use statsmodels Logit or sklearn LogisticRegression; split data before fitting preprocessing; report calibration and discrimination separately.
challenges.acceptance: No leakage from post-outcome variables; outcome prevalence and split strategy stated; performance metrics include uncertainty or caveats.
challenges.safety: Small event counts make complex models unstable. The 400-row dataset is educational, not for clinical deployment.

challenges.title: Diagnostic test evaluation
challenges.scenario: Calculate sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios and prevalence effects from a 2×2 table.
challenges.tasks: Given a hypothetical screening test and reference standard, calculate all core accuracy measures and explain how PPV/NPV change with prevalence.
challenges.method: Use a supplied 2×2 case and a prevalence-sensitivity table. Verify formulas independently.
challenges.acceptance: All four cells and denominators are shown; PPV/NPV are correctly tied to the specified prevalence; confidence intervals or uncertainty caveats included.
challenges.safety: Do not treat a screening test as a diagnosis; reference-standard imperfections matter.

challenges.title: Epidemiology and study design
challenges.scenario: Distinguish cross-sectional, case-control, cohort and randomised designs; calculate incidence, prevalence, risk, rate and person-time.
challenges.tasks: Select measures appropriate to each design. Calculate cumulative incidence and incidence rate from a synthetic cohort; identify selection, information and confounding biases.
challenges.method: Complete design-selection scenarios and compute risk, risk difference, risk ratio, odds ratio and person-time incidence rate.
challenges.acceptance: Every measure has a defined numerator, denominator, time frame and unit; design limitations correctly described.
challenges.safety: Prevalence is not incidence. Odds ratios approximate risk ratios only under specific conditions.

challenges.title: Survival analysis and time-to-event data
challenges.scenario: Handle censoring, Kaplan–Meier estimates, log-rank comparisons and Cox proportional hazards models.
challenges.tasks: Estimate event-free survival over time, compare two groups, interpret hazard ratios and assess proportional hazards conceptually.
challenges.method: Use lifelines if installed or R survival/survminer; document censoring and risk tables. Provide a Kaplan–Meier figure and Cox model summary.
challenges.acceptance: Time origin, event definition, censoring, at-risk population and follow-up horizon are explicit; hazard ratio interpretation is correct.
challenges.safety: A hazard ratio is not a risk ratio. Informative censoring and non-proportional hazards can bias interpretation.

challenges.title: Clinical research reporting and reproducibility
challenges.scenario: Produce a concise analysis report with a prespecified question, cohort flow, methods, results, tables, figures, limitations and reproducible code.
challenges.tasks: Create a mini statistical analysis plan and report using the synthetic cohort. Include a STROBE-aligned checklist for observational analyses and a reproducibility manifest.
challenges.method: Run the end-to-end Python script; produce outputs, record software versions and preserve code/data provenance.
challenges.acceptance: A reviewer can reproduce tables and figures from the supplied data and script; results distinguish planned from exploratory analyses.
challenges.safety: STROBE is a reporting guideline, not a study-quality scoring tool or proof of validity.

challenges.title: Sample size, power and precision
challenges.scenario: Understand effect size, alpha, power, variance, allocation ratio, attrition and precision-based planning.
challenges.tasks: Calculate an illustrative two-group sample size for a continuous outcome under stated assumptions; vary effect size and SD to observe sensitivity.
challenges.method: Use statsmodels.stats.power or a transparent formula; document two-sided alpha, target power, allocation and attrition inflation.
challenges.acceptance: Assumptions and units are explicit; the result is labelled illustrative and not a substitute for protocol/statistician review.
challenges.safety: Do not calculate sample size from a desired p-value or use post-hoc observed power as evidence.

challenges.title: Integrated clinical research client simulation
challenges.scenario: Deliver an end-to-end observational analysis with cohort description, primary outcome, adjusted model, sensitivity analysis and executive handoff.
challenges.tasks: In a 2-hour simulation, analyse synthetic blood-pressure follow-up data, define estimand and population, address missingness, model assumptions and clinical interpretation.
challenges.method: Use client-brief.md, rubric.json, Python/R starter scripts and the synthetic cohort dataset.
challenges.acceptance: Score at least 80/100 with no critical denominator, leakage, censoring or causal-claim errors.
challenges.safety: The dataset is synthetic and generated for teaching. No clinical effectiveness claim is supported.
